title: Work IQ: granular MCP policies to restrict platforms, workloads and operations
summary: The briefing accurately separates the planned granular policies from the documented tenant-level policy controls. The roadmap facts, admin path and billing statements are supported. Minor corrections should acknowledge conflicting Microsoft tool counts and remove the checklist's unmatched cost-management instruction.

claims.where: summary; controls[0]; What's changing; Why it matters; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The documented initial policy control is a tenant-wide on/off switch managed by tenant administrators.
claims.quote: In the initial release, Work IQ MCP provides tenant-level policy control. In the Microsoft 365 admin center, tenant administrators can turn Work IQ MCP policy on or off for the tenant.

claims.claim: Per-user, per-app, per-agent and scenario-specific templates are not part of the initial policy control surface.
claims.quote: Per-user, per-app, per-agent, or scenario-specific policy templates aren't part of the initial policy control surface.

claims.claim: Learn says more granular controls and policy templates might be added later.
claims.quote: More granular controls and policy templates might be added later based on customer requests, feedback, and usage.

claims.claim: Work IQ's policy layer uses Rego.
claims.quote: The policy layer uses Rego, the policy language from Open Policy Agent (OPA), to express authorization rules.

claims.claim: Rego is the policy language of Open Policy Agent.
claims.quote: The policy layer uses Rego, the policy language from Open Policy Agent (OPA), to express authorization rules.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Policy evaluates MCP tool requests at request time and can allow or deny them.
claims.quote: It adds a request-time governance layer that can allow or deny specific MCP tool requests based on tenant policy.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Mutation operations, including create, update, delete and sending email, are not allowed by default.
claims.quote: By default, mutation operations aren't allowed for safety. This restriction includes create, update, delete, and action requests that modify data, such as sending email.

claims.claim: Administrators can enable supported mutation scenarios through tenant policy.
claims.quote: Administrators can enable supported mutation scenarios through tenant policy in the Microsoft 365 admin center when those capabilities are needed.

claims.claim: A saved policy change can take up to 24 hours to apply across the tenant.
claims.quote: After you save the setting, it can take up to 24 hours for the policy change to apply across your tenant.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Work IQ MCP tools access mail, calendar, files, people, chat and sites.
claims.quote: 10 generic tools that provide direct access to Microsoft 365 data (mail, calendar, files, people, chat, and sites) and the ability to act on that data.

claims.claim: Work IQ MCP exposes ten generic tools.
claims.quote: The Work IQ MCP collapses hundreds of operations into just 10 generic tools
claims.fix: Replace 'through ten generic tools that work on resource paths' with 'through generic tools that work on resource paths'. The cited overview says 10, but https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/work-iq/mcp/overview lists 12 tool names across its Entity, Copilot and Schema rows.

claims.claim: The generic tools operate on resource paths and support reading and changing Microsoft 365 data subject to policy.
claims.quote: These tools function as simple verbs (such as fetch, create, and update), while resource paths define what the agent is working with.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: Policy cannot grant access beyond the signed-in user's existing access.
claims.quote: Policy can't grant access beyond what the signed-in user is already allowed to access.

claims.claim: Data access scope is among the default policy guardrail areas.
claims.quote:
The default policy provides guardrails for common Work IQ MCP scenarios. The exact policy behavior can depend on tenant configuration, but the main control areas are:
Data access scope | Which Microsoft 365 resource paths MCP tools can access

claims.claim: Data retrieval limits involving bounded collection reads are among the default guardrail areas.
claims.quote: Data retrieval limits | Whether collection reads are bounded to reduce large-scale data extraction risk

claims.claim: Policy complements rather than replaces Entra authentication, OAuth permissions and user permissions.
claims.quote: For Work IQ MCP, policy governance doesn't replace Microsoft Entra authentication, OAuth permissions, or the signed-in user's existing Microsoft 365 permissions.

claims.claim: Policy evaluates the requested resource path.
claims.quote: Path | The resource path being accessed, such as a mail, calendar, Teams, file, or people resource path

claims.claim: Policy evaluates the requested operation.
claims.quote: Operation | The requested operation, such as read, create, update, delete, action, or function

claims.claim: Policy evaluates request content.
claims.quote: Request content | Details in the request body or query parameters, when applicable

claims.claim: Policy evaluates tenant context.
claims.quote: User and tenant context | Information used to apply tenant-level governance rules

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Tenant policy can deny requests even when authentication and the required OAuth permission are present.
claims.quote: For developers, these controls mean an MCP request can fail because of tenant policy even when the user is authenticated and the app has the required OAuth permission.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft advises treating policy-denied responses as governance decisions.
claims.quote: Treat policy-denied responses as governance decisions, not transient failures to retry automatically.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Work IQ cost can be managed in Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: Work IQ cost is variable based on usage and can be managed in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: Copilot-licensed users get Work IQ in Microsoft 365 Copilot experiences and agents, with usage billing for custom and third-party agents.
claims.quote: For Microsoft 365 Copilot licensed users, Work IQ is available in all Microsoft 365 Copilot experiences and agents. It is subject to usage-based billing for custom and third-party agents.

claims.quote: Users without a Microsoft 365 Copilot license are billed based on usage.

claims.claim: The policy procedure requires an account permitted to manage tenant-level Work IQ or Copilot settings.
claims.quote: Sign in with an account that has permission to manage tenant-level Work IQ or Copilot settings.

claims.claim: The cited policy procedure does not name a specific administrator role.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ MCP policy manage role permissions administrator. Read Policy governance for Work IQ MCP; it specifies permission to manage tenant-level settings but no named role. The Business Applications access-control result concerns server availability, not this policy setting.

claims.claim: Microsoft advises checking tenant access and account permissions when policy settings do not appear.
claims.quote: If you don't see the Work IQ MCP policy settings, check that your tenant has access to Work IQ MCP and that your admin account has the required permissions.

claims.claim: The Work IQ service principal is automatically created on first use.
claims.quote: The Work IQ service principal is created automatically in the tenant when you use Work IQ for the first time.

claims.claim: Policy configuration before any MCP use can fail because the service principal has not been provisioned.
claims.quote: In some corner cases, such as configuring Work IQ MCP policy in the Microsoft 365 admin center before any MCP use in the tenant, the service principal might not exist yet and policy configuration can fail.

claims.claim: Tenant administrators can provision the service principal using the linked Enable your tenant for Work IQ steps.
claims.quote: Tenant administrators can provision it by following the steps in Enable your tenant for Work IQ.

claims.claim: The policy article discusses configuration experiences and editable policies.
claims.quote: If your experience configures policy settings, update only editable policies and validate values before sending updates.

claims.claim: The article describes toggle-style values such as Allowed and Disallowed.
claims.quote: Toggle-style settings use values such as Allowed and Disallowed.

claims.claim: Migration guidance says tenant-wide blocking stops Work IQ MCP for the entire tenant.
claims.quote: Block Work IQ MCP tenant-wide only when you intend to stop it for the entire tenant.

claims.claim: The migration article itself does not give the path for tenant-wide blocking.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ MCP policy settings API endpoint PowerShell; Work IQ MCP policy manage role permissions administrator. Read the full migration article: its rollback step names tenant-wide blocking without navigation steps; another search result documents server availability separately.

claims.claim: Policy approval does not guarantee success because user permissions are checked separately.
claims.quote: Policy approval doesn't guarantee the operation succeeds. If policy allows an MCP tool request, the underlying resource access is still checked against the signed-in user's Microsoft 365 permissions.

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Every control the governance checklist asks readers to review has a corresponding controls-table row.
claims.quote: Checklist: 'Review Work IQ usage and cost in the Microsoft 365 admin center'. Table: 'Whether Work IQ MCP policy applies to the tenant' and 'Per-platform, per-workload, per-agent or per-operation MCP restrictions'. Neither row covers cost management.
claims.fix: Remove the final After rollout bullet, 'Review Work IQ usage and cost in the Microsoft 365 admin center, where Learn says Work IQ cost can be managed.' Keep the supported cost-management statement in Cost and licensing.
